title: UK Student Visa Finances, ATAS and the Graduate Route Explained
seoTitle: UK Student Visa: Finances, ATAS and the Graduate Route
seoDescription: Keep UK Student visa finances, ATAS and the Graduate route separate, with official sources, evidence checks and clearly explained calculations.
intro: Financial evidence, ATAS and post-study permission are separate parts of planning a UK degree. Read the current requirements for your course and application date, and budget beyond the minimum visa evidence.
description:
Financial evidence, ATAS and post-study permission are separate parts of planning a UK degree. Read the current requirements for your course and application date, and budget beyond the minimum visa evidence.

Financial evidence and your everyday budget are different

GOV.UK sets minimum financial evidence for Student visa applications. Your CAS records course-fee information, while a separate requirement can apply to living costs. The amount and evidence rules depend on your circumstances, including whether an exemption applies.

As checked in October 2026, the published living-cost requirement is £1,529 per month in London or £1,171 outside London, for up to nine months. These are visa-evidence figures, not a forecast of what every student will spend. Recheck the official page when preparing your application, particularly for a later intake.

Build a separate budget for rent, insurance or healthcare-related charges, transport, food and initial moving costs. Check how scholarship payments align with deposits and expenses that arrive before the course starts.

Check whether you need ATAS

The Academic Technology Approval Scheme applies to specified study or research subjects and applicants covered by its rules. It is not required for every master's or PhD. Your university can help identify the course information needed, but you must check the official guidance for your nationality and circumstances.

Where ATAS is required, follow the instructions for the research description and course details. Allow time in your application plan and ask the university before changing information that may affect an existing certificate.

Understand the Graduate route separately

The Graduate visa is a separate application after successful completion of an eligible course. It is not included automatically with a Student visa. Under current published guidance, non-doctoral applicants applying on or after 1 January 2027 receive 18 months; a PhD or other doctoral qualification has a three-year period.

Eligibility, timing and application conditions still apply. Temporary permission to work is not a guarantee of later sponsorship or settlement. Some scholarship conditions also require recipients to return home, so read the funding agreement before planning to stay after graduation.

Keep the sources close to your application

Check official requirements again before submitting, rather than relying on a saved article or an older intake guide. Your university's international student advisers can help interpret the steps relevant to your course. Immigration decisions depend on the rules and evidence for the individual application.

Keep the three decisions separate

Admission, visa approval and permission to remain after graduation are different decisions. An academic offer does not confirm your immigration outcome, and an available post-study route does not change your current Student conditions. Make one checklist for financial evidence, another for ATAS if applicable, and a third for any later route you may consider. Use the relevant official pages for your application date. If the university gives guidance that appears inconsistent with the government instructions, ask its immigration team to clarify the exact rule and circumstances before you act.

Build three checklists with different deadlines

Financial evidence, ATAS and the Graduate route concern different stages. Financial evidence supports the relevant Student application. ATAS, where required, concerns specified study or research and applicants covered by the scheme. The Graduate route is a later application after successful completion of an eligible course. Keeping them in one vague visa checklist makes it easier to confuse a future option with a present requirement.

For every item, record the official source, the action required and the date by which you need it. Ask the sponsoring university about course-specific information, such as the research description needed for ATAS. Do not shorten or alter a technical description without checking whether it must match the university's approved information.

A financial-evidence example using the published amounts

At the time checked, GOV.UK lists £1,529 per month in London or £1,171 outside London, for up to nine months where the living-cost requirement applies. Multiplying gives £13,761 and £10,539 respectively for nine months. These figures are living-cost evidence only: course fees and other application costs must be considered separately. Recheck the official amount for your actual submission date, particularly for a later intake.

ItemWhat it establishesWhat it does not establish
CAS fee informationCourse and fee details recorded by the sponsorThat every visa requirement is already satisfied.
Financial evidenceCompliance with the applicable evidence rulesThat the minimum amount will cover your actual lifestyle.
ATAS certificate, if neededApproval under that scheme for the relevant study or researchA Student visa or an academic funding award.
Graduate-route eligibilityA possible separate application after completionA guaranteed job, sponsorship or permanent residence.

Where ordinary cash evidence is used, check the applicable holding-period and document-date rules. If support comes from a scholarship or student loan, read the evidence requirements for that category instead of assuming a personal bank statement is always the right document.

Do not budget a future route as current income

An available Graduate route can create time to seek work, but it does not fund the degree you are starting. Keep the course budget based on confirmed resources. If a scholarship includes conditions about returning home or accepting other funding, read those terms alongside your post-study plans.

Under the published Graduate guidance, non-doctoral applications from 1 January 2027 have an eighteen-month period, while qualifying doctoral graduates have three years. The application and eligibility conditions still apply. Use the current official page when you reach that stage, rather than relying on the duration advertised when you first considered the course.

Is ATAS required for every PhD?

No. Check the subject and applicant rules with the official guidance and the university's international team. A doctoral title alone does not answer the question.

Are visa maintenance figures university cost estimates?

No. They are application-evidence requirements. Build a separate city-specific budget for rent, bills, transport and the costs of moving before deciding whether the course is affordable.

Official sources and further reading

Requirements and policies should be checked for your programme and application date. Sources checked on 19 October 2026.

  • GOV.UK: Student financial evidence
  • GOV.UK: ATAS guidance
  • GOV.UK: Graduate visa
